source_text: quod invitemus ad dulcia furta, quibus Apostolum recitamus dicentem: Scio quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum
pass_a_gloss: That/which invitemus to dulcia furta, to-whom apostle recitamus dicentem: knows because not habitat in me, this is in in-flesh my, good.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports that Julian accused him of inviting people to pleasurable illicit acts by reciting the apostle: ‘I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh’ (Romans 7:18).

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
